en.html:
I move to the wall, out of the way, and watch Tamura's people at work. Enthusiasm in every movement. Not one person working with a yawn.

Win this Yamato GP, the first unified national championship since the war, and a place in Yamato's armor-racing history is assured. A monument that will not weather away.

Such commitment, then, is only natural.

But—is it my imagination?

Something faintly <ruby>negative<rt>・</rt></ruby> hangs in the team's excitement. Not only the glory ahead they seem to be watching. Behind them, too, as though some carnivorous shadow is closing in.

That sort of atmosphere.

Lose here and the team disbands—has something like that been proposed? I have heard nothing of it...

ja.html:
邪魔にならないよう壁際に退避して、タムラの人々
の作業を見守る。
　一つ一つの挙措に熱意が感じられた。欠伸をしつつ
手を動かしている者など一人もいない。

　今回の大和ＧＰ――戦後初の国内統一選手権で勝利
を収めれば、間違いなく大和における装甲競技の歴史
上に不朽の名を刻むことになる。
　決して風化しない金字塔だ。

　それを思えばこの意気込みもむしろ当然と思える。
　
　だが――錯覚であろうか。

　タムラチームを包む熱気には、かすかに<ruby>負<rt>・</rt></ruby>の匂いが
ある。
　前方に輝く栄光だけを見ているのではない。同時に、
後方から迫る肉食獣の影に怯えているような――

　どこか、そんな気配があった。
　この大会に敗れたら解散、というような話でも持ち
上がっているのだろうか？　聞いたこともないが……。

en.html:
Chachamaru"Why start talking to you otherwise? These people want their racing pure, that's all."
Kageaki"...?"
Chachamaru"They don't want money・ following them onto the track. Preparing a race machine costs money, fine. Nobody's arguing. But line up on the grid, cross the finish—between those two, let us forget it."
Chachamaru"Let the spectators forget also."
Kageaki"............Are there moves in that direction・・・・・・?"
Chachamaru"Moves? Full movement. Such a tasty dish, you think the money-hungry fellows will leave it alone?"
Kageaki"Armored competitionarmor racing is among Yamato's most popular sports at present..."
Kageaki"If they successfully turned it into gambling・・・, the profits could be enormous."
Chachamaru"Exactly that."
Kageaki"Tamura opposes it, then?"
Chachamaru"Nichimo and Yugen too. Among manufacturers, that's about the list. Most of the independent teamsprivateers side with Tamura."
Kageaki"And in favor?"
Chachamaru"Everybody else, frankly. Shokyo at the center. Apparently they've already drawn up the management committee. Half their own people, of course. Why leave control to chance?"
Kageaki"Yokotan also supports it?"
Chachamaru"Their top man resisted at first. Folded finally. What to do? Stand up to Shokyo, perhaps. But who stands behind Shokyo—that gives a man pause."
Kageaki"...Their connectionsbacking."
Chachamaru"Shokyo's president has an elder sister. Her husband's a samurai commander serving our esteemed Yamato GP organizer."
Kageaki"The organizer... Lieutenant General Raichou Imagawa, the Oyumi Kubo?"
Chachamaru"For one company, rather a heavy opponent, wouldn't you say?"
Kageaki"I cannot disagree."

en.html:
Kubo can mean a Rokuhara military commander or his headquarters. Strictly speaking, kanrei is the former, kubo-fu the latter.

Four such headquarters stand in Kanto: Koga and Oyumi in Shimousa, Horigoe in Izu, and Sasagawa in Aizu. Each holds both military and civil authority over its strategically vital surrounding region. Above them, only the head of the shogunate: the <ruby>Commander of the Six Guards<rt>Rikue Taishoryo</rt></ruby>.

The Muromachi Tandai in Kyoto, the Dazaifu in Kyushu and the Chinjufu in Mutsu are their formal equals. Actual power, however, none has to match a kubo-fu. A class apart, the four Kanto Kubo.

Rokuhara's top leadership, in short. The Four Heavenly Kings, as the thoroughly worn-out expression has it. With such a connection, Shokyo must be breathing very confidently indeed.

〝公方〟とは六波羅の軍司令官、もしくはその隷下の
司令部を指す。
　正しくは前者を管領と云い、後者を公方府と云うが。

　公方は下総古河、下総小弓、伊豆堀越、会津篠川の
関東四点に設置され、それぞれに枢要である周辺地域
一帯において軍政両権を掌握する。
　彼らの上には幕府の長たる<ruby>六衛大将領<rt>りくえたいしょうりょう</rt></ruby>が在るのみだ。

　これと格式上は同等の存在として京都の室町探題、
九州の大宰府、陸奥の鎮守府があるが、いずれも公方
府ほどの実権力は備えていない。
　関東四公方は別格の存在であるといえる。

　つまりは六波羅幕府の首脳。垢じみた表現を用いて
四天王などとも称される最高幹部だ。
　翔京がこれと繋がっているのなら、その鼻息はさぞ
荒いことだろう。

en.html:
The mystery clears. This is why such an unusual cloud of tension hangs over Tamura Works' garage.

Lose this battle, lose armor racing as a sport. Everyone here must share that understanding.

I look at Misao Oji, still polishing her part. However often I look, small she remains.

On that small back she carries her father's dream and the hopes of those who love racing as she <ruby>flies<rt>runs</rt></ruby>. No burden? Impossible to believe.

Yet in her clear expression I can find no fear, no wavering, not even fatigue. Only something single-minded.

　後には中腰のまま呆然とする俺だけが残された。

　……思えば、そもそも。
　彼女はどうして、俺にあのような話をしたのだろう。

　何故あのように親しげだったのだろう？
　過去に面識はないと思うのだが……。

　首を傾げるべき点は多かったが、ここで思い悩んで
いてもどうにもなりそうにない。
　俺は皇路親子に挨拶をして、ガレージを出た。

　時間は有限だ。
　他の場所も見て回らなくてはならない。
